messages:
Priya Nair: Hi folks 01st day and getting my MBP (M2) set up. I9m stuck on Jamf enrollment: the installer finishes but System Settings still shows "MDM profile pending installation" and FileVault setup never completes. Tried twice. Any quick checks?

Marco IT: Welcome Priya! :wave: Can you paste the output of `sudo tail -n 60 /var/log/jamf.log` and `sudo fdesetup status`? Also which network are you on (home vs office)?

Priya Nair: On home WiFi. fdesetup says: `FileVault is Off.` Jamf log tail below:
```
2026-04-02 09:03:12.001 jamf[6789]: Enrollment: user-initiated
2026-04-02 09:03:18.214 jamf[6789]: ProfileInstallation: started
2026-04-02 09:03:20.332 jamf[6789]: EscrowService: sending escrow request
2026-04-02 09:03:21.789 jamf[6789]: EscrowService: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
2026-04-02 09:03:21.790 jamf[6789]: MDMProfileInstallationError: Escrow failed (403)
2026-04-02 09:03:21.791 jamf[6789]: BootstrapToken: not present
```

Onboarding Bot: Auto: new-device-enroll attempt logged for device SER12345 at 2026-04-02T09:03:12Z - status: failure (Escrow 403)

Riley Chen: 403 usually means the enrollment token on our server rejected the request (token mismatch or user not allowed). Quick question: did you sign in to Okta/SSO during the flow or skip it?

Priya Nair: I clicked the "Sign in with Okta" button and completed SSO. The browser returned to System Settings but no confirmation dialog popped up except "MDM profile pending installation".

Marco IT: Ok. Two likely causes: 1) the bootstrap token wasn't created because this device did the enrollment from the non-OS-Setup path (user-initiated), or 2) our enrollment token rotated and your enroll flow used a cached token. First try: reboot and enroll again, but before enrollment open System Settings > Privacy & Security and ensure there are no blocked system extension prompts.

Priya Nair: Rebooted, verified no blocked prompts, retried, same 403 and "BootstrapToken: not present" in log.

IT Ops: Thanks for the log. We rotated a short-lived enrollment token earlier for a security roll; some user-initiated enrolls can fail until the client fetches the new token. Since FileVault is off we need either: A) perform a supervised DEP-style enrollment (requires factory reset) or B) we push a one-time Jamf policy that generates a personal recovery key and forces escrow. Option B is less disruptive. Priya, will you be near the office network in ~15-30 mins? If not, we can push it over the internet but you might need to accept an extra prompt.

Priya Nair: Not at the office today. Can you push remotely? I9m available.

IT Ops: We can. We'll create and push a transient policy that runs `fdesetup add -personalrecoverykey -keychain` and then calls the Jamf binary to escrow. This will prompt you to enter your local admin password once. To avoid issues, please temporarily disconnect from any VPN and keep the laptop awake. ETA ~10 minutes.

Riley Chen: Also sending a temporary Okta action to add your device to the allowed enroll list just in case the 403 is an allowlist hit.

Priya Nair: Okay disconnecting VPN now.

IT Ops: Pushed policy at 09:20. You should see a Jamf notification; if a prompt appears for admin password please enter it so the PRK can be created and escrowed.

Priya Nair: Saw the Jamf prompt, entered my admin password. Getting a macOS prompt: "Allow Jamf to make changes?" and then a spinner.

Marco IT: Good sign. Waiting on enrollment callback.

IT Ops: Console shows PRK created and escrowed for SER12345. Also updated device record to mark bootstrap token not required for this enrollment path.

Priya Nair: System Settings now shows "MDM profile installed" and FileVault is turning on. `sudo fdesetup status` now: `FileVault is On.` :tada:

Marco IT: Nice! Welcome to the team Priya. If you want, we can schedule a quick check-in to pair on installing dev tooling.

Priya Nair: That would be great, thanks everyone!
